messages:
sec-bot: [ALERT] High rate of SSO backup-code usage detected for user kate@acme.corp — 5 attempts within 3m, 3 failures, 2 successes. IPs: 185.65.13.4, 2.58.123.9. Rule: detect-backup-code-abuse triggered.

alex: seeing it, assigning. Which accounts beyond kate?

maria: tagging @oncall — do we have a quick containment play?

sec-bot: currently only kate@acme.corp and one service account svc-deploy@acme.corp. Service account attempts from 54.37.22.1 (AWS EC2 range). kate attempts show impossible-travel flags (US -> DE in 4m).

samir: force global sign-out for kate and svc-deploy now. Also rotate their SSO session tokens and mark backup codes as invalidated. I'll open INC-4087.

jess: do we need KMS key rotation? the SSO app uses a client secret plus signed assertions; keys look intact in initial audit. I'd prefer rotating client secret for the SSO app after containment instead of full KMS rotation.

alex: running quick audit query on auth logs for kate and svc-deploy:
```
SELECT timestamp, event, ip, user_agent, outcome
FROM auth_events
WHERE user IN ('kate@acme.corp','svc-deploy@acme.corp')
AND timestamp > now() - interval '24 hours'
ORDER BY timestamp;
```
Results: 12 attempts for kate over last 30m, 5 distinct IPs, 2 successful (today 12:03, 12:07 UTC), geo hops DE/US/BR. svc-deploy shows 3 attempts from 54.37.22.1 - failed OTP.

samir: blocking the two malicious IPs at edge WAF and adding temporary rate-limit on backup-code submission (5/min -> 1/min). Creating INC-4087: "SSO backup-code abuse / impossible travel - ACME". Assigning to sec-response.

jess: note: impossible-travel plus backup-code success is suspicious for credential sharing or leaked codes. Do we have logs of backup-code issuance/last-used timestamp? Need to check audit log and support ticket history.

oncall: executing session revoke for kate@acme.corp and svc-deploy@acme.corp: `authctl sessions revoke --user kate@acme.corp --reason "suspected compromise"` and same for svc-deploy. Applied. Also disabled backup-code auth method for kate pending reset.

sec-bot: updated: 2 more automated attempts stopped by rate-limit, no further successful logins. Detection score degraded from CRITICAL -> HIGH.

maria: do we notify the customer (acme) now, or wait for triage? Support prefers heads-up that we've contained and are rotating credentials.

alex: suggest customer-safe notification: "We detected suspicious access attempts against two identities and took containment actions (sessions revoked, backup codes invalidated). We're investigating and will update." Drafting email for legal review.

samir: post-containment checklist (to do): 1) rotate SSO client secret for ACME tenant 2) audit RBAC changes for any new admin grants in last 72h 3) check KMS access logs for any asymmetric key usage by those identities 4) enforce stricter backup-code rate-limit and introduce cooldown 5) add anomaly alert for backup-code success from new geo within 1h 6) run credential-exposure scan on public repos 7) prepare customer comms and PSP if PII accessed.

jess: adding runbook items: update docs for backup-code revocation flow, surface nicer UX for forced backup-code reset to reduce support friction.

alex: opening follow-up tasks under INC-4087 and linking to runbook. Will keep this thread for comms. :white_check_mark:
